title: Mexico Details El Chapo Isidro Capture: No Civilian Deaths Reported; Four Soldiers and Seven Suspected Gunmen Killed
author: Mexico Solidarity Media
content:
No civilian deaths were reported in the operation to capture El Chapo Isidro
in Sinaloa, which left four soldiers and seven suspected gunmen dead.

According to [La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/21/politica/defensa-
confirma-muerte-de-cuarto-soldados-y-7-presuntos-criminales-en-operativo-
contra-el-chapo-isidro), gunmen fought for more than five hours to prevent the
cartel leader’s removal, firing at troops and helicopters, burning vehicles
and blocking roads. The four soldiers killed were traveling in a convoy sent
to reinforce the operation.

The Secretariat of National Defense said Army and National Guard special
forces carried out the capture with support from Mexican and US intelligence
agencies.

Describing the approach in a [statement reproduced by El
Informador](https://www.informador.mx/mexico/defensa-confirma-detencion-del-
chapo-isidro-en-sinaloa-20261121-0035.html), Defensa said:

> “Using stealth and surprise, through different ground access routes to the
> arrest area.”

The forces established:

> “An internal and external security deployment to prevent escape or the
> arrival of reinforcements.”

According to the statement, troops entered the house after coming under
gunfire and explosive attacks.

Also captured were Germán “N,” known as Serafín, identified as the
organization’s second-in-command, and José “N,” its financial operator. The
three were flown to Mexico City and handed over to prosecutors.

Defensa identified Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, as a
Beltrán Leyva leader allied with the Sinaloa Cartel’s Los Mayos faction. It
said he faced an arrest warrant in Mexico and an extradition order to the
United States.
